metaTitle: Permanent vs Seasonal Holiday Lighting: Which to Pick
metaDescription: Compare permanent architectural LED lighting to traditional seasonal Christmas light installs, covering cost over time, timing, and ESA electrical safety.
h1: Permanent vs Seasonal Holiday Lighting: How to Choose
summary: Comparing app controlled permanent LED lighting to traditional seasonal Christmas light installation on cost, timing, and electrical safety in Ontario.
intro: Ontario homeowners now have two genuinely different ways to light a house for the holidays, and increasingly for the rest of the year too. One is the traditional seasonal service, a crew installs string lights in late fall and takes them down in the new year. The other is permanent architectural lighting, fixtures mounted once along the roofline that stay there year round and are controlled through an app to display any colour combination, including but not limited to holiday patterns. Neither option is objectively better, they suit different budgets, timelines, and how much you actually want your house lit up in July. This guide breaks down what each option involves, how the cost comparison plays out over several years rather than one season, when to book installation, and the electrical safety considerations that matter with any lighting connected to your home's power.

blocks.text: Traditional seasonal lighting service is what most people picture when they think of a professional holiday light install, C9 or mini string lights clipped along the roofline, gutters, and sometimes trees or shrubs, installed by a crew in the weeks before the holiday season and removed and stored, often by the same company, once the season ends. Many companies offer to store the lights over the summer and reinstall the following year, which removes the hassle of ladder work and storage for the homeowner but means the display exists only for that window each year.

Permanent architectural lighting, sometimes called permanent LED lighting or year round lighting, uses individually addressable LED fixtures mounted once along the roofline, soffits, or architectural features of the home. Because each light or small cluster of lights can be controlled independently through a smartphone app, the same fixed hardware can display warm white for everyday accent lighting, red and green for Christmas, orange for Halloween, or essentially any colour and pattern combination for a birthday or a local team's game night, all without anyone touching a ladder after the initial install.

items: Seasonal service: installed and removed each year by a crew, typically active for a few weeks around the holidays only
Permanent lighting: installed once, controlled by app, usable year round for holidays, everyday accent lighting, and special occasions

blocks.text: The upfront cost comparison favours seasonal service clearly, a single season of professional installation and takedown is a much smaller expense than a permanent lighting system, which involves purchasing and mounting fixtures along the full length of roofline or architectural features being lit, along with the control hub and any electrical work needed to power it. This upfront gap is the main reason many homeowners default to seasonal service without considering the alternative.

Where the comparison shifts is over several years. Seasonal service is a recurring annual cost, install and takedown fees each year, plus a smaller cost each year for burnt out bulbs or damaged strings, and that recurring cost continues indefinitely with no endpoint. Permanent lighting is a larger cost concentrated in year one, but LED fixtures rated for exterior architectural use are typically built to last many years with minimal maintenance, so from that point forward the ongoing cost is largely just electricity, which is modest given how efficient LED lighting is, plus occasional fixture replacement if a section fails.

Get a specific quote for both options based on your actual roofline length rather than relying on general cost comparisons you find online, since every home's linear footage, roof complexity, and existing electrical capacity changes the math meaningfully.

The other cost factor worth naming honestly is usage. A seasonal display gets used for a few weeks a year no matter what you paid for it. A permanent system gets used far more often, for the holiday season certainly, but also for everyday dusk lighting, other holidays, and one off occasions, which changes how you should think about cost per use rather than cost per season alone. Homeowners who want their house lit only at Christmas and are not interested in year round use will generally find seasonal service the more sensible choice regardless of the multi year math.

Seasonal lighting companies in Ontario get busy well before most homeowners start thinking about the holidays, and booking early, often in late summer or early fall, is the best way to get your preferred installation date and avoid being squeezed into the crew's busiest weeks in November and early December. Installation itself typically happens in cooler but not yet frozen weather, since crews need workable conditions on ladders and roofs, and companies generally will not install once significant snow or ice accumulation makes roof access unsafe.

Permanent lighting installation is less weather sensitive in terms of when it can happen, since it is a one time mounting job rather than a seasonal setup, but it still benefits from being scheduled outside of the depths of winter given the exterior electrical connections and ladder work involved. Many homeowners choose to have permanent lighting installed in spring, summer, or early fall specifically so the system is fully operational and tested well before the first holiday season it will be used for, rather than trying to have both the mounting and the electrical hookup done in the same rushed window seasonal companies are working in.

items.title: Decide on your system by late summer
items.text: Whether choosing seasonal service or permanent lighting, deciding early gives you access to better installation dates and avoids the fall rush.

items.title: Book seasonal installers well before November
items.text: Seasonal lighting companies fill their calendars quickly once fall arrives, so early booking often means more flexibility on installation date and crew availability.

items.title: Schedule permanent lighting installation outside peak winter
items.text: Spring through early fall installation allows time for the system to be fully tested before the holiday season arrives, avoiding a rushed first use.

items.title: Confirm takedown or off season plans
items.text: For seasonal service, confirm removal timing and storage. For permanent lighting, confirm what maintenance, if any, is recommended before the next heavy use season.

blocks.text: Any lighting system that connects to your home's electrical supply, rather than simply plugging into an existing exterior outlet, falls under the oversight of the Electrical Safety Authority, Ontario's regulator for electrical work. Permanent lighting systems in particular often involve a dedicated circuit, a control hub wired into the home's electrical panel or a nearby junction, and exterior rated wiring run along the roofline, all of which should be installed by a licensed electrical contractor and, where required, permitted and inspected through the ESA process.

This is one of the clearest places where choosing an installer based purely on price can go wrong. A company that mounts permanent lighting fixtures without involving a licensed electrician for the electrical connection, or that skips the ESA notification and inspection process where it applies, is taking a shortcut that can create a genuine fire or shock hazard, and it can also create problems with your home insurance if an incident occurs and the electrical work cannot be shown to have been done to code.

Seasonal string lighting is generally lower risk from an ESA standpoint since it typically plugs into existing exterior outlets rather than requiring new permanent wiring, but it still deserves attention to basics: outlets used should be ground fault circuit interrupter protected for exterior use, extension cords should be rated for outdoor use and not run through standing water or snow in a way that creates a hazard, and any professional installer should be using connections and clips rated for exterior conditions rather than improvising with household grade materials.

items: Ask whether a permanent lighting system requires new wiring into your electrical panel, and if so, confirm a licensed electrician is doing that work
Ask whether ESA notification or inspection applies to your specific installation and confirm the installer is handling it
For seasonal lighting, confirm exterior outlets used are ground fault circuit interrupter protected
Confirm any extension cords or connectors used outdoors are rated for exterior conditions
Ask what happens if a fixture or connection fails, is there a warranty and a clear process for service

blocks.text: Whichever direction you choose, ask directly about licensing and ESA compliance before signing anything, this is not a place to assume every installer handles it the same way. Our directory at /winners can help you find contractors recognized for reliable, code compliant installation work, and /resources has our full library of guides if you want to compare other exterior home projects before deciding where holiday lighting fits into your budget this year.

checklist: Decide whether you want a display only for the holiday season or year round accent lighting use
Compare a specific quote for seasonal service against a specific quote for permanent lighting, based on your actual roofline
Book seasonal installation early, ideally by late summer or early fall, to secure your preferred date
Schedule permanent lighting installation outside peak winter so it can be tested before first heavy use
Ask whether permanent lighting requires new panel wiring and confirm a licensed electrician handles that work
Confirm whether ESA notification or inspection applies to your installation and that the installer manages it
For seasonal lighting, confirm exterior outlets are ground fault circuit interrupter protected
Ask about fixture and connection warranty terms for permanent systems
Confirm storage and reinstallation terms if choosing a seasonal service that stores your lights
Get the full scope, including electrical work where applicable, in writing before paying a deposit

faq.q: Is permanent lighting actually cheaper in the long run than seasonal service?
faq.a: It can be, since permanent lighting concentrates cost in year one and then mostly just involves electricity and occasional fixture upkeep, while seasonal service is a recurring annual cost. The comparison depends on your roofline size and how many years you plan to stay in the home, so get specific quotes rather than assuming.

faq.q: Can permanent lighting really be used for more than just Christmas?
faq.a: Yes, that is one of its main advantages. Because the fixtures are individually app controlled, the same hardware can show warm white everyday accent lighting, other holiday colours, or custom patterns for a birthday or event, all without any physical reinstallation.

faq.q: Do I need an electrician for permanent lighting, or can any lighting installer do it?
faq.a: Any work involving new wiring into your electrical panel or permanent exterior circuits should be done by a licensed electrical contractor, and may require Electrical Safety Authority notification or inspection depending on the scope. Ask your installer directly how the electrical portion of the job is being handled.

faq.q: When should I book seasonal holiday light installation?
faq.a: Booking in late summer or early fall generally gives you the best chance at your preferred installation date, since seasonal lighting companies fill their calendars quickly once November arrives and stop installing once winter weather makes roof access unsafe.
